claims.text: Every note covers: the reason for the encounter and relevant history, exam findings and prior test results; the assessment, clinical impression or diagnosis; the plan for care; and the date and your legible identity.
claims.quote: The documentation of each patient encounter should include: reason for encounter and relevant history, physical examination findings, and prior diagnostic test results; assessment, clinical impression, or diagnosis; plan for care; and date and legible identity of the observer.
claims.locator: General principles of medical record documentation, item 2

claims.text: History parts: chief complaint (CC), history of present illness (HPI), review of systems (ROS), and past, family and/or social history (PFSH).
claims.quote: Each type of history includes some or all of the following elements: Chief complaint (CC) History of present illness (HPI) Review of systems (ROS) and Past, family, and/or social history (PFSH).

claims.text: Where they go: the CC, ROS and PFSH can be written as separate sections or worked into the HPI.
claims.quote: The CC, ROS and PFSH may be listed as separate elements of history, or they may be included in the description of the history of the present illness.

claims.text: Chief complaint: a concise statement of the symptom, problem, condition, diagnosis, recommended return or other reason for the encounter, usually in the patient's own words.
claims.quote: The CC is a concise statement describing the symptom, problem, condition, diagnosis, physician recommended return, or other factor that is the reason for the encounter, usually stated in the patient's own words.

claims.text: HPI: a chronological story of the present illness, from the first sign or symptom (or from the last encounter) to now.
claims.quote: The HPI is a chronological description of the development of the patient's present illness from the first sign and/or symptom or from the previous encounter to the present.

claims.text: PFSH: past history (illnesses, operations, injuries and treatments); family history (medical events in the family, including hereditary or risk-raising diseases); social history (an age-appropriate review of past and current activities).
claims.quote: The PFSH consists of a review of three areas: past history (the patient's past experiences with illnesses, operations, injuries and treatments); family history (a review of medical events in the patient's family, including diseases which maybe hereditary or place the patient at risk); and social history (an age appropriate review of past and current activities).

claims.text: Complete PFSH, all three areas: new outpatient patients, observation, initial inpatient care and consultations need at least one item from each of past, family and social history.
claims.quote: DG: At least one specific item from each of the three history areas must be documented for a complete PFSH for the following categories of E/M services: office or other outpatient services, new patient; hospital observation services; hospital inpatient services, initial care; consultations; comprehensive nursing facility assessments; domiciliary care, new patient; home care, new patient.

claims.text: Complete PFSH, two areas: established outpatient patients and the emergency department need at least one item from two of the three areas.
claims.quote: DG: At least one specific item from two of the three history areas must be documented for a complete PFSH for the following categories of E/M services: office or other outpatient services, established patient; emergency department; domiciliary care, established patient; and home care, established patient.

claims.text: No history available: describe the patient's condition or the circumstance that keeps you from getting one.
claims.quote: DG: If the physician is unable to obtain a history from the patient or other source, the record should describe the patient's condition or other circumstance that precludes obtaining a history.

claims.text: Exam, affected systems: write the specific abnormal and relevant negative findings; "abnormal" alone isn't enough.
claims.quote: DG: Specific abnormal and relevant negative findings of the examination of the affected or symptomatic body area(s) or organ system(s) should be documented. A notation of "abnormal" without elaboration is insufficient.

claims.text: Exam, everything else: describe abnormal or unexpected findings in asymptomatic areas; for normal unaffected areas, a brief "negative" or "normal" is enough.
claims.quote: DG: Abnormal or unexpected findings of the examination of any asymptomatic body area(s) or organ system(s) should be described. DG: A brief statement or notation indicating "negative" or "normal" is sufficient to document normal findings related to unaffected area(s) or asymptomatic organ system(s).
